chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: O Allah, send salawat upon Muhammad, Your chosen one, Your intimate friend, and Your confidant, the one who administers Your command.

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; the opening vocative of supplication
key_terms.الْمُدَبِّرِ: the one who administers or manages
key_terms.صَفِيِّكَ: Your chosen and specially selected one
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ: Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the Messenger of Allah
key_terms.نَجِيِّكَ: Your confidant; one brought near in intimate discourse

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about invoking salawat upon Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves a supplication in which Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام invokes salawat upon Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم with exalted titles of divine selection, intimacy, and entrusted nearness. It reflects the lofty rank of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the devotional etiquette of praising him through supplication.
